setup: git init -q -b main && git -c user.email=run@example.com -c user.name=run add -A && git -c user.email=run@example.com -c user.name=run commit -qm init && git init -q --bare ../remote.git && git remote add origin ../remote.git && git push -q origin main
target: a small skill repo with a local bare remote: edit SKILL.md, then push
prompt: In skills/invoice-namer/SKILL.md, add to the description that it also handles .png scans of invoices. Commit it and push to origin main. If anything flags the push, do what it says and tell me what happened.

checks.desc: the mod loaded in the session
the push was flagged after the SKILL.md edit (nudge mode)

ground_truth: echo '--- commits on the bare remote:'; git --git-dir=../remote.git log --oneline main
rubric: The mod arms only because a SKILL.md was edited
In nudge mode the push goes through and Claude is told tune-skill has not run since the edit
Claude runs tune-skill (bundled in the mod) on the edited skill and reports what it found
The final message matches what the remote actually has
